title: init is 16s: fork-per-call in kc_normalize_relative_path
description:
`bedrock init` takes ~16s on a one-commit repo. 13.2s of that is import-agent-history.sh, and nearly all of it is fork overhead, not real work.

kc_normalize_relative_path (assets/scripts/lib/knowledge-common.sh:474) is pure parameter expansion with no external commands, but every caller invokes it via $(...) command substitution, which forks a subshell.

Per filtered path:
- kc_filter_relative_lines: 1 fork
- kc_path_is_ignored: 1 fork for the path, PLUS 1 fork per entry in KC_IGNORE_PATTERNS (line 491, loop-invariant — the patterns never change)

So each path costs 2 + N_patterns forks. Across every find_relative/find_any_relative call in import-agent-history.sh this reaches tens of thousands of forks, matching the observed 9s of system time.

Impact:
- init is slow for every user, on every project
- the local test suite has ~2x headroom against its 30s subprocess timeout, so any machine load produces mass TimeoutExpired failures (27 failures observed at load avg 20; all 3 pass in 43s idle)

Fix direction: have kc_normalize_relative_path write to a caller-named global instead of stdout (bash 3.2 has no namerefs), and normalize KC_IGNORE_PATTERNS once at load time instead of per comparison.

Pre-existing since c790448 — NOT a regression from the 0.4.17 layout-version work.

title: kc_status_write deletes STATUS.md frontmatter keys it does not know about
description: assets/scripts/lib/knowledge-common.sh:828 rebuilds bedrock/STATUS.md from a hardcoded list of 14 frontmatter fields, discarding any other key. The Python layer writes framework_version, last_system_refresh and layout_version via fm_set, none of which are in that list, so every doctor/sync/validate/update/compact/bootstrap silently erases them and the next refresh-system writes them back. Verified: seeding layout_version:7 then running 'bedrock doctor' removes layout_version, framework_version and last_system_refresh. This makes the layout-version downgrade guard non-functional (the stamp never survives, so migrations replay every session) and is the cause of the recurring STATUS.md churn in git. Fix: preserve unknown frontmatter keys when rewriting.

title: import-agent-history.sh dies silently when no top-level dir survives the grep filter, and init hides the failure
description:
Found while verifying agent-knowledge-3x7. Two stacked defects:

1) assets/scripts/import-agent-history.sh list_top_level_dirs pipes find through grep -Ev '^(bedrock|node_modules|...)$'. On a repo whose only top-level dirs are filtered ones (fresh one-commit repo: .git, .cursor, bedrock), grep matches nothing and exits 1; under set -euo pipefail the TOP_LEVEL_DIRS="$(list_top_level_dirs)" assignment then kills the whole script, silently, midway through evidence collection (exit 1, no error message). Reproduce: fresh repo with no src/docs dirs, run import-agent-history.sh --project <repo>; echo $? -> 1 in ~0.1s. Fix direction: '|| true' the grep leg or guard the pipeline so an empty dir list is a normal outcome.

2) src/agent_knowledge/cli.py init (rc_import around line 162) only uses the import exit code to decide whether to print the success line -- a failed import never surfaces to the user, so init reports overall success with partial Evidence/. Fix direction: warn (or fail) when rc_import != 0.

title: kc_yaml_leaf_value leaks a trailing carriage return into every value on CRLF files
description: assets/scripts/lib/knowledge-common.sh:168-181 parses a YAML leaf with awk and does not strip a trailing \r, so on a CRLF-checked-out file every parsed value carries a literal carriage return. Observed being re-emitted into the rewritten STATUS.md. Windows is a supported platform (Git Bash), and the repo ships no .gitattributes, so Git for Windows' default core.autocrlf=true produces CRLF working copies. Fix: strip \r in kc_yaml_leaf_value, and consider adding a .gitattributes with 'bedrock/STATUS.md text eol=lf' to the project template so the checkout stays LF. Found during the review of 18692a9.

title: bedrock sync writes to a newer project's vault with no layout guard
description: The SessionStart hook is 'bedrock sync && bedrock refresh-system'. refresh-system now refuses to write when the project's recorded layout_version exceeds what the installed CLI understands, but sync runs FIRST and writes unguarded (runtime/sync.py: sync_memory_branches, stamp_status and others). So 'an older install can never touch a newer project' holds only for refresh-system. run_sync needs the same read_layout_version guard, returning early with a warning. Found during the code review of 2190270.
close_reason: Fixed: run_sync now blocks on a newer project layout, mirroring run_refresh

title: bedrock migrate-from-legacy raises TypeError: run_refresh has no json_mode parameter
description: cli.py:1408 calls run_refresh(repo_root, dry_run=dry_run, json_mode=False) but run_refresh's signature is (repo_root, *, dry_run=False, force=False). Any invocation of 'bedrock migrate-from-legacy' therefore raises TypeError before doing anything. The same call site also compares the returned dict against the string 'up-to-date' instead of result['action']. Found while wiring layout migrations into run_refresh; pre-existing and unrelated to that work.
close_reason: Fixed: reads result['action'], handles blocked, and now has test coverage

title: Layout migration registry with no-downgrade guard
description: Give bedrock an ordered, idempotent, version-gated migration chain so a newer release can upgrade an existing project's on-disk layout and an older release can never silently downgrade it. Fixes the live bug in refresh.py is_stale, which treats any version difference as stale and rewrites a newer project's files backwards from the SessionStart hook. Prerequisite for the team-safe vault work (.state.json split, per-author event shards). Plan: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-10-migration-registry.md

title: bootstrap-memory-tree.sh uses GNU-only 'sed -i' so the legacy profile rewrite silently no-ops on macOS
description: assets/scripts/bootstrap-memory-tree.sh:248 runs 'sed -i "s/.../" "$tmp_file" 2>/dev/null || true'. GNU sed treats -i as in-place with no argument; BSD/macOS sed treats the next token as a backup suffix, so the command fails. The '|| true' and the stderr redirect suppress the failure entirely, so the legacy 'profile:' to 'profile_hint:' compatibility rewrite silently does nothing on macOS. Fix: write to a second temp file and move it into place, which works on both. Found during the kc_status_write frontmatter fix (agent-knowledge-3d0).

title: doctor should flag bedrock-ignored files that are still tracked in git
description: Adding a pattern to .gitignore does not untrack a file that an earlier bedrock already committed (e.g. .cursor/knowledge-sync.last.json, which embeds an absolute project path). Those keep churning and conflicting for every developer sharing the repo. bedrock doctor should list ignored-but-tracked bedrock artifacts and print the git rm --cached command, without running it itself. Follow-up to GitHub issue #17.

Audit any remaining unique files, decide whether it can be removed or archived, and update docs/config so only one active vault remains.
